request: Add a connecting hole of 1.7 millimetre diameter and apply 0.1 millimetre grooves to increase grip and prevent slipping.

parameters.direction: Along the common transverse axis of the two clevis ears
parameters.extent: Through both clevis ears and across the intervening fork gap
parameters.placement: Concentric with the existing coaxial clevis pin-bore geometry

actions.target: The coaxial transverse connecting-hole location through Clevis ear A and Clevis ear B. The existing cylindrical pin-bore surfaces provide the clearest functional and geometric localization. The finished bore must pass through both ears on one common axis so that a single connecting pin can be inserted through the complete clevis.
actions.relational_constraint: The hole must connect the two otherwise separated clevis ears across the central fork gap. Its axis must be coaxial through both ears, normal to the planar cheek faces, and centered on the existing rounded lug crowns. Ear A and Ear B must retain equal alignment about the central gap.
actions.unresolved_reference: Resolved by interpreting 'connecting hole' as the clevis pin connection defined by the existing coaxial bore geometry. Because the multiview images already show openings in both ears, the current bore feature must first be measured. If it is not 1.7 millimetres, suppress or replace the existing bore feature rather than placing a redundant smaller cut inside an already larger opening.
steps: Activate Clevis ear A, section S04, and Clevis ear B, section S05, as the working regions. Use cylindrical bore faces 0026 and 0031 to recover the current pin-bore axes and verify that they are coincident.

Measure the existing bore diameters and inspect their feature history. If the current holes are already 1.7 millimetres in diameter, retain the geometry and convert the dimension into an explicit controlled parameter. If they differ, suppress the original hole or cut feature where feature history is available.

If direct feature suppression is unavailable and the existing openings are larger than 1.7 millimetres, heal or locally rebuild the ear solids before recutting; a 1.7 millimetre subtractive cut cannot reduce the diameter of an existing larger opening.

Select the planar outer cheek of one clevis ear, preferably face 0028 on Ear A, as the sketch support. Alternatively, create a datum plane coincident with that cheek and normal to the recovered common bore axis.
Project the circular edges of cylindrical face 0026 into the sketch and constrain a new circle concentrically to the projected bore center and the rounded crown represented by face 0027.
Dimension the sketch circle to 1.7 millimetres diameter. Fully constrain its center to the recovered common axis so that no independent positional degrees of freedom remain.
Create a through-all subtractive extrusion or hole feature normal to the sketch plane. Set the extent to pass through Ear A, the open fork gap, and Ear B, terminating beyond outer cheek face 0033.
Where the CAD system supports scoped cuts, include only the solids or connected regions belonging to S04 and S05. Do not extend the cut into the shoulders S02 and S03 or into the central spine S06.
Confirm that the resulting cylindrical portions replacing faces 0026 and 0031 are one common 1.7 millimetre bore, with no axial step or offset at either ear.

Inspect the minimum ligament between the new bore and rounded crowns 0027 and 0032, as well as the ear-root transitions. Preserve the existing crown and root fillets unless a manufacturing edge break is required.
Regenerate the model and verify the hole in the left, right, top, and top-right isometric views. Perform an axis-coincidence and through-clearance check using a 1.7 millimetre gauge cylinder.

parameters.pattern: Shallow radial face-serration pattern concentric with the connecting-hole axis
parameters.application: Symmetric on the two opposing inner clevis cheeks
parameters.manufacturing_method: Shallow engraved or subtractively cut grooves

actions.target: The opposing planar inner cheek faces of Clevis ear A and Clevis ear B that contact and laterally constrain the mating link inside the fork gap. These faces are the most functionally appropriate anti-slip surfaces because they directly interface with the connected component.
actions.relational_constraint: The grooves must be applied symmetrically to the opposing inner cheek faces, remain concentric with the 1.7 millimetre connecting-hole axis, preserve the coaxial bore, and avoid the ear perimeter, root blends, and critical bore-bearing surface. Groove depth must be directed outward into each ear so that the fork gap is not obstructed.
actions.unresolved_reference: Resolved by interpreting 0.1 millimetres as groove depth and by locating the grip treatment on the opposing inner fork faces. Groove count, angular spacing, and groove width were not explicitly stated; use a uniformly spaced radial pattern compatible with the available cheek area and the intended manufacturing process.
steps: Complete and validate the 1.7 millimetre connecting-hole operation before creating the groove features so that the final bore axis can drive the serration pattern.
Select Ear A inner cheek face 0029 as the first sketch plane. Project the finished bore opening, the rounded ear perimeter, and the ear-root boundaries into the sketch as construction references.

Create two construction circles concentric with the connecting-hole axis to define the inner and outer limits of the grooved annulus. Keep the inner limit clear of the bore edge to preserve pin-bearing material, and keep the outer limit clear of crown and root fillets.

Sketch one narrow radial groove slot between the construction circles. Fully constrain the slot radially to the bore axis and ensure that it does not intersect the cylindrical bore face 0026 or any external ear edge.
Create a shallow pocket cut normal to face 0029 with a depth of 0.1 millimetres, directed into the material of Ear A and away from the central fork gap.

Circular-pattern the seed groove about the connecting-hole axis to form evenly spaced radial serrations. Select a conservative groove count and spacing that leave continuous lands between grooves and do not materially weaken the ear.

Repeat the same construction on Ear B inner cheek face 0034, using cylindrical face 0031 as the concentric reference. Reverse the cut direction so the 0.1 millimetre pockets enter Ear B rather than protruding into the fork gap.

Align the two groove patterns angularly unless an alternating pattern is required by the mating component. Maintain equal depth and matching radial limits on both inner cheeks to preserve symmetric contact behavior.

Do not place grooves on outer cheeks 0028 and 0033, rounded crowns 0027 and 0032, or inside bore faces 0026 and 0031. Grooving the bore could damage the connecting pin or interfere with the intended pin-bearing function.
Apply only a minimal edge deburr if required by the manufacturing process. Do not add a large chamfer that would remove the sharp groove edges responsible for increased grip.
Inspect the modified fork gap for adequate mating-part clearance and verify that the grooves do not create disconnected sliver faces or intersect the ear-root blends.

Regenerate the model and check the groove depth, symmetry, bore continuity, and remaining ear wall thickness. Confirm through contact or interference analysis that the serrated cheek faces improve resistance to relative slipping without obstructing pin installation.

intention: Provide a controlled 1.7 millimetre transverse connection through both clevis ears.
Increase grip at the mating-link contact faces.
Prevent slipping or relative rotation of the component held within the clevis gap.
Preserve coaxial pin alignment and the structural load path through both ears and their supporting shoulders.
